content: TFAM, also known as mitochondrial transcription factor A or mtTFA, is a protein encoded by the TFAM gene in humans. This protein plays a critical role in mitochondrial function. The TFAM gene encodes a transcription factor that is essential for activating mitochondrial transcription. It also participates in the replication of the mitochondrial genome. TFAM binds to mitochondrial promoter DNA, facilitating the transcription of the mitochondrial genome. Research conducted in mice has demonstrated that the product of the TFAM gene is necessary for regulating the copy number of the mitochondrial genome. Furthermore, it is indispensable for embryonic development. When the expression of this gene was specifically disrupted in heart and muscle cells in a mouse model, it resulted in a condition resembling Kearns-Sayre syndrome. Structurally, TFAM is classified as a double box high-mobility group (HMG) protein. It has DNA-binding and DNA-bending properties, which are critical for its function. In terms of molecular interactions, TFAM has been shown to interact with TFB1M, another mitochondrial transcription factor.
